clauses.reason: The approval clause says the President does "do order that the said code of fair competition be and it is hereby approved", and that "my order of approval is subject to the following condition". That is a section 3(a) approval of the Code of Fair Competition of the Newsprint Industry, with the one condition addressed in the next clause and no stated period for the approval itself. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) repealed the provisions of Title I delegating power to the President to "approve or prescribe codes of fair competition" and "providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; the resolution states no effective date other than its approval ("Approved, June 14, 1935."), so the approval stopped operating on June 14, 1935. Under section 3 of Title I (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3) an approved code had legal effect only through 3(b) standards of fair competition, 3(c) injunctions and 3(f) misdemeanor penalties, all of which the repeal removed. Schechter (SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERJDG, May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.

The condition directs that "within 90 days from the effective date of this code the Administrator hold such further hearing upon such notice as he, in his discretion, shall fix for the purpose of determining the adequacy of the minimum wages established in said code", after which "his report and recommendation shall be submitted to me for further order, which order shall have the effect of a condition to my approval of this code". It is a condition of the approval (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3, section 3(a)): the only effect of the contemplated further order is to be a condition of the approval, and the hearing is directed only to test the minimum wages "established in said code". The 90-day period is a deadline measured from an effective date no held source states, and a deadline is not an end. No held record shows the hearing held, a report made or a further order issued under this order's own text, so no earlier end by performance is established. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) repealed the provisions of Title I delegating power to the President to "approve or prescribe codes of fair competition" and "providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; the resolution states no effective date other than its approval ("Approved, June 14, 1935."), so the approval stopped operating on June 14, 1935. Under section 3 of Title I (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3) an approved code had legal effect only through 3(b) standards of fair competition, 3(c) injunctions and 3(f) misdemeanor penalties, all of which the repeal removed. Schechter (SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERJDG, May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. With the approval gone on June 14, 1935 there was no approval left for a further order to condition, and the condition stopped operating with it.

inventory_overrides.reason: Operative approval and the statement that the approval is subject to a condition; the preamble recites the application and findings and commands nothing.
The separate command directing the Administrator to hold a further hearing on minimum wages and report for a further order; it is a distinct command from the approval.

research_rationale:
Identity and page check: the held text for EO 6435 is the American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 362261), registered as grade mirror_transcription (not an original). Its page record is a Common Crawl capture of 2025-01-17T18:13:50Z whose heading names Executive Order 6435, whose date (November 17, 1933) and subject agree with the text, and whose text sha256 equals the held text's. The WPA 1944 list row (1933 Nov 17 p.551: Code of Fair Competition for the Newsprint Industry approved. III NRA Codes 103.) confirms the order's date and subject. The order approves a code of fair competition under section 3(a) of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, so the reviewed shared analysis (SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and review-shared/ADJUDICATION.json) applies: a code-dependent command that did not end earlier ended on June 14, 1935 by statutory repeal (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2); Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date. The machine inventory had one clause covering both the approval and the condition; it is corrected into two clauses (the approval, and the hearing-and-report condition) so each command has its own end.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved Code of Fair Competition of the Newsprint Industry before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences that the repeal did not turn into continuing commands; nothing in S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) continues the approval after June 14, 1935. Any antitrust exemption for complying action before the repeal (NIRA section 5, SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5) is likewise an accrued effect; the resolution's proviso, which extends the exemption only to "agreements and action thereunder" meeting stated conditions, leaves open how far it narrowed the exemption for past action, so the claim records no continuing exemption and no surviving approval. Any hearing held, report made or further order issued under the condition before the repeal is an accrued act, not a continuing command.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935: the Court held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional and the Live Poultry Code provisions in question invalid. Recorded as a validity characterization for every section 3 code approval, not as this order's end; the judgment did not cancel or withdraw this order.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 3; the provisions described were repealed on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2).
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 3 (48 Stat. 195, June 16, 1933): under 3(a) the President approved codes and could impose conditions of approval; under 3(b), 3(c) and 3(f) an approved code's provisions became standards of fair competition enforceable by injunction and as misdemeanors. These are the legal effects that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 5; S.J. Res. 113 (June 14, 1935) limited the exemption by proviso; the held text does not settle the proviso's effect on past action.
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 5 exempted from the antitrust laws any code approved and in effect under Title I and any complying action while Title I was in effect and for sixty days thereafter; any exemption for action taken before the repeal is an accrued effect, not continued operation of the approval.
